description: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two pruning methods—“Per-Output” (blue bars) and an unlabeled method represented by orange bars—across sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%, as evaluated in the context of DLP (Dynamic Layerwise Pruning) in large language models. The horizontal axis, labeled “Sparsity Rate,” displays discrete categories at 10% intervals, while the vertical axis, labeled “Perplexity,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10¹ to 10³, with major gridlines at 10, 100, and 1000. At low sparsity rates (10%–50%), both methods exhibit low and nearly identical perplexity values, hovering just above 10. As sparsity increases to 60% and 70%, perplexity rises moderately for both, with the orange bars consistently showing slightly higher values than the blue “Per-Output” bars. At 80% sparsity, both methods experience a sharp increase in perplexity, with the blue bar reaching approximately 500 and the orange bar exceeding 800, indicating a significant degradation in model performance at high pruning levels. The chart visually emphasizes the growing divergence between the two methods as sparsity increases, with the orange bars consistently taller than the blue bars beyond 50% sparsity, suggesting the “Per-Output” method may better preserve model quality under aggressive pruning.
